boundary_reason: One bounded destructuring assignment operation within the Go language; it does not replace a multi-operation language subsystem.
caller: A Go developer processing optional heterogeneous arguments in NewExtParam(value interface{}, opts ...interface{}).
input: An array or variadic sequence; concrete initial example is opts ...interface{}, plus an ordered list of destination variables.
output: Separate destination variables receive available sequence values from left to right; destinations past the input length receive a null/nil value.
limits: Only the initial heterogeneous options example and stated array/variadic boundary are fixed. The text does not resolve the static type of a missing value for every possible typed array.
Extra source elements do not require extra destinations; only specified destinations are assigned.
The long strconv/type-switch example illustrates existing caller processing, not a requirement that the supplier perform numeric parsing.
No speed target, concurrency guarantee, general pattern matching or generics requirement is supplied.

source_sections.heading: Proposal: requested assignment and existing processing example
Costs and named PHP list analogy

named_component_roles.PHP list: Explicit existing analogy for the same value-retrieval use; rediscovery is not a new target.
named_component_roles.strconv.ParseInt: Existing downstream type conversion, outside the destructuring action.

whole_must.requirement: Provide a Go-level array/variadic destructuring assignment that binds separate destination variables without caller-written per-element length/index checks.
whole_must.falsifying_input: In a Go function with opts=[]interface{}{7,"x"}, attempting a three-variable destructuring still requires the caller to implement len(opts) checks and opts[i] extraction.

whole_must.requirement: Assign the supplied destinations in left-to-right source order, and do not require more destinations than the caller specified.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Input [10,20,30] with two destinations produces (20,10), rejects the unused third value, or requires a third destination.

whole_must.requirement: For the heterogeneous options boundary, produce nil/null for a destination beyond the source length so the caller can test it.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Input [10] with three interface-valued destinations panics, rejects the arity mismatch, or yields non-null fabricated values in positions two and three.

partial_must.requirement: Extract an ordered fixed-width group of values from an array/variadic-like sequence without the caller implementing individual element extraction.
partial_must.falsifying_input: For [10,20,30] and width two, the component only exposes raw indexing and requires the adapter to implement the extraction loop.

partial_must.requirement: Preserve left-to-right values, truncate unused trailing source positions, and pad missing heterogeneous positions with null/nil.
partial_must.falsifying_input: For input [10] and width three the result is not (10,null,null), or for [10,20,30] and width two it rejects rather than returning the first two values.

independent_partial_purpose: Prepare a fixed-width, null-padded tuple of optional argument values for validation before Go language syntax is integrated.
independently_useful_next_action: The caller can check the three extracted option positions for nil and perform the existing per-type processing.
remaining_adapter: Bind the prepared positions to Go variables and integrate any new compiler syntax/type rules; retain caller-specific numeric/type conversions. An adapter that implements sequence extraction or missing-value padding itself does not establish partial completion.
preferences: The example syntax is sz, sc, pr := opts...; punctuation is an illustrated syntax preference, while the assignment semantics are mandatory.
Less code clutter and easier understanding are motivations, not measured performance predicates.
false_same_name_criterion: A list API that appends values, enumerates variable names, or returns a string representation does not perform ordered destructuring with missing-position nulls, even if it is named list/unpack.
neutral_query: array variadic destructuring assign variables left to right missing elements null
a_queries: array destructuring fixed number variables missing values null extra elements
variadic arguments unpack optional values null padding assignment

boundary_reason: A complete benchmark-unit metadata protocol spanning producers, in-band and command-line representations, parser conflict handling, forward propagation, consumer direction/statistical semantics and tool integration.
caller: A benchmark producer and a consumer/comparison tool such as benchstat handling custom measurement units.
input: Benchmark results plus unit-name/key/value metadata supplied in the result stream or through a command-line flag.
output: A consistent per-unit interpretation of beneficial direction and statistical assumptions, applied to subsequent benchmark measurements; conflicting properties produce an error.
limits: Behavior for benchmark results preceding a unit declaration is explicitly unspecified.
Streaming consumers must not be forced to buffer all results merely in case a later property appears.
Normal-distribution support is deliberately omitted; no such mandatory requirement may be added.
The author expresses no strong opinion on exact syntax; Unit/key=value and -unit are concrete proposed representations, not an exclusive punctuation requirement.

source_sections.heading: Motivation: custom unit properties and benchstat
In-band and CLI representations and alternatives

named_component_roles.benchstat: Explicit intended consumer family; returning benchstat itself is already named, while a distinct previously unnamed component inside that family must be separately identified.
named_component_roles.Go benchmark format: Explicit existing format; the linked older format proposal is prior context, not this sampled event.

whole_must.requirement: Carry per-unit key/value properties through both benchmark-stream declarations and an equivalent tool command-line configuration, and expose them to benchmark consumers.
whole_must.falsifying_input: A custom text-bytes property supplied through a CLI option cannot reach the comparison tool, or only an unrelated benchmark-name tag is produced.

whole_must.requirement: Reject conflicting properties specified for the same unit.
whole_must.falsifying_input: The same unit is declared higher=better and lower=better, and the consumer silently accepts both or overwrites one without an error.

whole_must.requirement: Apply a declaration to all following benchmark results with that unit; allow streaming without requiring retrospective buffering.
whole_must.falsifying_input: After a custom-unit declaration, a later result uses no property or a different property, or the parser cannot emit earlier results until end of input.

whole_must.requirement: Support all four higher/lower combined with better/worse formulations and interpret beneficial direction consistently.
whole_must.falsifying_input: higher=better and lower=worse are treated as opposite meanings, or one of the four allowed forms is rejected.

whole_must.requirement: Support assume=nothing and assume=exact with nothing as default; nothing uses nonparametric treatment and exact does not require repeated sampling to increase confidence.
whole_must.falsifying_input: An omitted assumption forces a normal model, or a file-size unit marked exact is rejected for lacking repeated samples.

partial_must.requirement: Parse a unit declaration/configuration into a unit-keyed property record usable by a benchmark tool.
partial_must.falsifying_input: Unit text-bytes lower=better assume=exact yields only raw text and requires the adapter to implement the unit/property parser.

partial_must.requirement: Normalize all four direction forms and the nothing/exact assumptions, preserving nothing as the default.
partial_must.falsifying_input: lower=worse is not recognized as larger-is-better, or omitting assume does not produce the nothing/default interpretation.

partial_must.requirement: When merging declarations for one unit, signal contradictory properties as an error.
partial_must.falsifying_input: Merging higher=better with lower=better for ns/op silently succeeds.

independent_partial_purpose: Validate and normalize benchmark-unit declarations into a usable per-unit metadata map before integrating them with a complete result stream and comparison UI.
independently_useful_next_action: A benchmark consumer can inspect the normalized direction/assumption map, reject conflicts, then use it when interpreting subsequent results.
remaining_adapter: Connect normalized records to the CLI and stream producers, apply them to following benchmark records, and wire their meanings into statistical/reporting consumers. If the adapter must implement the property parser, normalization or conflict rule, the component has not completed the partial action.
preferences: Unit and -unit key=value spellings are proposed concrete syntax; alternative equally expressive spellings are not automatically conflicts.
Built-in examples ns/op lower=better and MB/s higher=better illustrate expected defaults; no universal fixed list of units is specified.
false_same_name_criterion: A physical-unit conversion API that converts metres to feet, or a test-runner unit label, does not supply benchmark direction/assumption metadata or conflict/propagation semantics.
neutral_query: benchmark result unit metadata higher lower better statistical assumptions exact nonparametric
a_queries: benchstat custom benchmark unit properties higher lower better assume exact
benchmark unit metadata key value parser conflicting properties command line streaming

boundary_reason: A bounded change to the concurrent-map-write failure branch within the runtime; it does not redesign the map subsystem or the request-serving protocol.
caller: A Go runtime map-assignment path and an application/API request handler that has a recovery boundary.
input: A map write attempted while the runtime concurrent-write detection condition is true; initial code uses h.flags & hashWriting in mapassign_fast64.
output: A catchable panic for the detected concurrent map write, enabling a recovery boundary to contain the failure and respond to the affected request instead of immediately terminating the service.
limits: The author acknowledges correct map access should use a mutex; this request concerns handling a detected misuse, not making unsynchronized maps safe.
The first text does not establish memory safety or map integrity after a race. Such guarantees must not be inferred.
The cited 90% preference is the proposer’s claim, not a measured acceptance criterion.
No behavior is specified for concurrent races the existing detector misses.

named_component_roles.panic/recover: Already explicit mechanism; merely rediscovering generic panic/recover documentation is not a new implementation of the requested map-detector behavior.
named_component_roles.mapassign_fast64: Exact actor shown in the first draft; generic application error wrappers do not replace this runtime branch.

whole_must.requirement: At the runtime concurrent-map-write detection branch, signal panic instead of an uncatchable fatal termination.
whole_must.falsifying_input: The hashWriting overlap branch still calls fatal, while only nil-map writes or unrelated application errors panic.

whole_must.requirement: Allow a valid recovery boundary to catch that specific concurrent-map-write panic and keep the process available.
whole_must.falsifying_input: A request handler with an applicable recover boundary still loses the whole service when the detector reports concurrent map writes.

whole_must.requirement: Preserve a failing/terminating path for code without a recovery boundary while permitting the recovering API caller to produce an error response such as HTTP 500.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Without recover the invalid write silently succeeds, or with recover the API cannot finish the affected request with an error response.

partial_must.requirement: Provide the actual map-detector-to-catchable-signal path for detected overlapping writes, rather than a generic panic helper outside the detector.
partial_must.falsifying_input: The component only offers recover() or an exception wrapper; Go’s concurrent-map-write branch still terminates via fatal.

partial_must.requirement: Demonstrate that the resulting signal can be caught at an appropriate recovery boundary without mandatory immediate process termination.
partial_must.falsifying_input: The component reports a concurrent-write error by process exit or an uncatchable runtime failure.

independent_partial_purpose: Contain the detected map-write failure as a recoverable runtime signal before adding request-specific response handling.
independently_useful_next_action: The application recovery boundary can log/translate the caught signal and finish the affected request with an error response.
remaining_adapter: Integrate the verified detector behavior into the target Go runtime/version and wire the application recovery boundary to request cleanup/HTTP error reporting. A generic wrapper that leaves fatal unchanged forces the adapter to implement the core action and fails partial completion.
preferences: HTTP 500 is the stated example of request containment, not a requirement for a particular web framework.
No requirement to restore a raced map to a valid state is invented.
false_same_name_criterion: A function named Panic or Recover operating on ordinary returned errors or nil-map writes has the wrong triggering input/actor if concurrent-map-write detection still invokes fatal.
neutral_query: Go concurrent map writes runtime fatal recoverable panic request recovery
a_queries: Go runtime concurrent map writes change fatal panic recover
Go map concurrent write detection catch panic HTTP request recovery

boundary_reason: An integrated Go-to-WebAssembly interoperability protocol: compiler export declaration, linker/instance export table, host-native argument preparation through memory/stack, and invocation across that boundary.
caller: A Go developer exposing a function and a JavaScript/WebAssembly host invoking the compiled function.
input: A Go function selected for export in a GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm build, a compiled module with its memory/stack interface, and native argument values; the concrete example is Bar(id int).
output: A directly exported WebAssembly instance symbol that the host can invoke after placing native values into the Go stack, with the Go function receiving the intended argument.
limits: The first text targets the js/wasm environment and does not require a standalone WASI environment.
The proposed compiler marker may be a directive or an instruction; exact //go:wasmexport spelling is an example.
Memory allocator access for strings/slices is mentioned as possibly needed, not a fully specified mandatory allocator API.
The abstract example’s stack offset and internal names are illustrative ABI details; no stable ABI guarantee is stated.
No numeric performance threshold or universal Go-type marshaller is required.

source_sections.heading: Mark functions and publish direct instance exports

named_component_roles.Wasmer: Explicit original background export/import reference; a returned Wasmer component needs novelty coding within this named family.
named_component_roles.DataView.setInt32: Explicitly shown as the native integer argument-preparation component; rediscovery for this same use is already named.
named_component_roles.wasm_exec.js: Existing bridge context; a generic JS callback wrapper alone does not satisfy direct export requirements.

whole_must.requirement: Provide a mechanism in the Go build/toolchain to select a Go function for a direct WebAssembly export.
whole_must.falsifying_input: The only supported path wraps the function in js.Func/js.Value and attaches it to globalThis; the compiler cannot emit a selected direct export.

whole_must.requirement: Publish the selected function as a host-addressable WebAssembly instance export alongside the module’s built-in exports.
whole_must.falsifying_input: The host can locate only built-in bridge symbols or a JavaScript global, not the selected Go function in the instance export table.

whole_must.requirement: Permit the host to prepare native argument values through the module’s Go memory/stack boundary, rather than limiting every argument to a wrapped js.Value.
whole_must.falsifying_input: For Bar(123), the host can pass only js.Value references, cannot reach the target stack memory, or writes an unrelated copy invisible to the Go function.

whole_must.requirement: Support invoking the directly exported function after argument preparation so the Go function observes the intended native value.
whole_must.falsifying_input: After placing integer 123 into the designated argument slot, invoking the export does not call Bar or Bar observes a different/uninitialized value.

partial_must.requirement: Write a supplied native 32-bit integer at a caller-specified byte offset in a view of WebAssembly linear memory using the example’s little-endian representation.
partial_must.falsifying_input: Given value 0x01020304 and a valid offset, the component cannot produce bytes 04 03 02 01 at that offset without the adapter implementing byte encoding/writing.

partial_must.requirement: Mutate the same memory buffer visible to the executing WebAssembly/Go module, so the prepared argument can be consumed by the subsequent export call.
partial_must.falsifying_input: The memory-writing operation changes a detached copy or ordinary JS object, leaving the module’s designated stack argument bytes unchanged.

independent_partial_purpose: Prepare the integer argument bytes for an already exported low-level function in the module’s memory, an independently usable host-side step before invoking that function.
independently_useful_next_action: Once the stack argument slot contains the intended integer bytes, the host can invoke an already known direct export.
remaining_adapter: Implement/choose the Go export declaration and linker integration, obtain the export and stack pointer, select the ABI-correct offset, and invoke the function. The adapter may choose addresses but must not implement the component’s core integer encoding/memory write. A memory writer alone does not satisfy the whole Go-export protocol.
preferences: Compiler directive //go:wasmexport and foo·Bar naming are illustrative choices.
Allocator access for complex strings/slices remains an open integration issue in this first text.
false_same_name_criterion: An export keyword that exports JavaScript module bindings, or a data-view API that formats values for display, has the wrong actor/output; neither emits a Go WebAssembly function nor writes its shared linear-memory argument slot.
neutral_query: Go WebAssembly export functions native values host memory stack calling exports
a_queries: Go WebAssembly direct function exports JavaScript stack memory native integer arguments
WebAssembly linear memory DataView setInt32 little endian exported function arguments
